title: ORGANIC LAW N° 002/2026.OL OF  25/05/2026 GOVERNING ELECTIONS

articles.heading: Purpose of this Organic Law
Interpretation In this Organic Law
articles.text:
(a) “Embassy of Rwanda” includes any
premises within the territory under the
jurisdiction of Rwanda’s diplomatic
mission abroad;
(b) “Ambassador” means a
representative of Rwanda to a foreign
State;
(c) “proclamation of election results”
means an official announcement of
election results made by the competent
authority on the basis of polling results
consolidated from all levels at which
the voting has taken place;
26
(d) “polling station” means a structure
designated by the Commission
comprising at least one polling room;
(e) “polling room” means a room
designated by the Commission where
persons eligible to vote and registered
on the voters’ register cast their votes;
(f) “national identity card” means a
physical or digital document
identifying a person, issued by the
competent authority;
(g) “voters’ register” means a document
containing the particulars of persons
eligible to vote;
(h) “invalid vote” means a vote cast by a
voter that bears signs other than those
prescribed for voting or that does not
bear any mark;
(i) “experienced person” means a person
who, over a prolonged period, has
performed substantial functions, and
has thereby acquired skills or
knowledge, through the performance
of various activities, that are relevant
27
to the duties attached to an elective
office;
(j) “electoral observer” means a
Rwandan or foreign national,
representing a national nongovernmental organisation, the
Rwanda Civil Society Platform, a
faith-based organisation, a State organ,
a State, an international or foreign
organisation, accredited by the
National Electoral Commission to
observe the electoral process;
(k) “electoral college” means a group of
persons who have the right to vote;
(l) “person of integrity” means a
Rwandan citizen of unimpeachable
character in personal behaviour and in
relationships with others;
(m) “election” means a process by which
a choice is made by voting;
(n) “direct election” means an electoral
system in which the voter personally
casts his or her vote;
28
(o) “indirect election” means an electoral
system in which the persons who have
the right to vote are represented, in the
casting of votes, by some of them;
(p) “Commission” means the National
Electoral Commission;
(q) “polling committee” means a
committee consisting of the presiding
officer of the polling station and
polling room coordinators;
(r) “declaration of polling results”
means the announcement of polling
results at the level at which polling is
conducted, made by the persons
responsible for conducting polling at
that level;
(s) “electoral campaign” means the
process by which an independent
candidate, a political organisation, or a
coalition of political organisations
promotes and presents its programme
for the purpose of securing election;
(t) “polling booth” means a designated
area within a polling room established
for the purpose of enabling the voter to
29
cast his or her vote in secrecy;
(u) “candidate’s agent” means a
Rwandan citizen registered on voters’
register mandated by a candidate to
monitor the electoral process on that
candidate’s behalf;
(v) “electoral coordinator” means a
person designated by the Commission
to be, at each relevant level of the
Commission, responsible for the
supervision and coordination of
electoral operations;
(w)“candidate” means any individual,
political organisation or coalition of
political organisations that, having
satisfied the prescribed requirements,
participate in electoral competition;
(x) “electoral volunteer” means a willing
and capable person appointed by the
Commission to participate, without
remuneration, in the preparation and
conduct of electoral operations;
(y) “poll clerk” means a person in charge
of polling operations within a polling
room;
30
(z) “level of the Commission” means a
polling room, polling station, District,
Province, the City of Kigali or the
country, at the level of which polling
takes place, and any other place
determined by the Commission;
(aa) “voter” means any Rwandan citizen
who has the right to vote.

articles.heading: Scope of application This Organic Law applies to the following elections
Organ in charge of elections (1) The organ in charge of elections is the Commission
articles.text:
(2) The Commission is responsible for
ensuring compliance with the laws
governing elections and issues, where
necessary, instructions required to
ensure the proper conduct of elections
in accordance with the provisions of
this Organic Law.
(3) For the purposes of discharging its
responsibilities, the Commission
appoints electoral volunteers.
(4) Instructions of the Commission
determine the procedures for the
appointment of, and requirements for,
electoral volunteers.

CONDUCT OF ELECTIONS IN

Section One: Voters’ register
33
(a) a person who has been deprived, by
competent courts, of his or her
right to vote and who has not been
rehabilitated or granted amnesty in
accordance with Law;
(b) a person convicted of intentional
homicide;
(c) a person convicted of the crime of

(d) a person who has been convicted of

(e) a person who has been convicted of

(f) a person incarcerated;
(g) a refugee.
(2) Every year and whenever necessary,

Authority transmits to the Commission

34

articles.heading: Obligation to register on the voters’ register
Eligible person for registration on the voters’ register and documents to be produced by him or her
Person ineligible for registration on voters’ register 4
Person responsible for registration on voters’ register and his or her duties (1) An electoral volunteer designated by the
articles.text:
Commission is responsible for registration
on the voters’ register in each Village and
at each Embassy.
(2) An electoral volunteer is responsible for
the following:
(a) to ensure that registration on the voters’
register is done in accordance with law;
(b) to keep the voters’ register and ensure
the security of materials in collaboration
with the administrative authorities of the
place of registration operation;
(c) to prepare a report on the voters’
registration operation;
(d) to perform any other election-related
duty as may be assigned by the

38
(3) Instructions of the Commission
determine procedures for the
implementation of the provisions of
Paragraphs (1) and (2).

articles.heading: Correction of voters’ register between the publication of the provisional and the final voters’ register
articles.text:
(1) The Commission corrects errors
identified after the publication of the
provisional voters’ register.
(2) Instructions of the Commission
determine procedures for the correction
of the voters’ register during the period
between the publication of the
provisional voters’ register and that of
the final voters’ register.

articles.heading: Publication of the list of persons removed from the voters’ register (1) The Commission, prior to the
articles.text:
publication of the final voters’ register,
publishes a list of persons removed
from the voters’ register on the
grounds provided for under Article 7.
(2) Instructions of the Commission
determine procedures for the
39
publication of a list of persons
removed from the voters’ register.

articles.heading: Maintenance of, and person authorised to access, voters’ register (1) The voters’ register is maintained in the
articles.text:
database of the Commission. A
candidate or any other person authorised
by the Commission is given access to a
copy thereof.
(2) Instructions of the Commission
determine procedures for the
maintenance of, and provision of access
to a copy of, the voters’ register.

articles.heading: Lodging of complaint relating to registration on voters’ register (1) Any interested person may lodge a
articles.text:
complaint relating to registration on the
voters’ register. However, the complaint
is admissible only if it is lodged prior to
the publication of the final voters’
register.
(2) The complaint is lodged in writing at the
level of the Commission having
jurisdiction over the area in which the
issue is identified.
40
(3) At the level of the Embassy of Rwanda,
the complaint is lodged in writing with
the electoral coordinator.

articles.heading: Procedures for resolution of a complaint relating to the voters’ register (1) The level of the Commission seised of a
articles.text:
complaint relating to the voters’ register
renders a decision within 48 hours of
receipt of the complaint. A copy of the
decision is issued forthwith to the party
concerned and, where necessary, the
voters’ register is immediately corrected
by way of additional registration or
deletion, in accordance with the
decision.
(2) Where the complainant is dissatisfied
with the decision, he or she appeals to
the next higher level of the Commission
within 24 hours of being notified of the
decision.
(3) At the level of the Embassy of Rwanda,
if the complainant is dissatisfied with the
decision of the electoral coordinator, he
or she appeals to the chairperson of the
Commission within 24 hours of being
notified of the decision.
41

articles.heading: Referral to the court against a decision relating to voter registration or correction of the voters’ register
articles.text:
A decision relating voter registration or the
correction of the voters’ register, rendered at
the final level of the Commission, may be
referred to the competent court. However, the
filing of such a complaint with the court has
no suspensive effect on the electoral process.
Section 2: Submission of candidacies and
electoral campaign

articles.heading: Person qualified to be elected A person is qualified to be elected if he or she – (a) has attained the age prescribed by law;
articles.text:
(b) is a person of integrity;
(c) is registered on the voters’ register;
(d) is not be subject to the restrictions
provided for under Article 7;
42
(e) has not been placed under guardianship
by virtue of an order of a competent
court;
(f) does not suffer from an illness of such a
nature as to prevent him or her from
fulfilling the functions related to the
office for which he or she seeks to stand
as a candidate;
(g) is no longer in active service in such a
capacity as member of the Rwanda
Defence Force, police officer, judge,
prosecutor, an investigator, a member
of the National Intelligence and
Security Service, of Rwanda
Correctional Service or of District
Administration Security Support
Organ;
(h) not have caused the insolvency of a
body corporate he or she directed,
unless he or she has been subject to
rehabilitation;
(i) not have been convicted by a final
judgment to a term of imprisonment of
6 months or more, unless he or she has
been rehabilitated;
43
(j) not have been dismissed from public
service, unless he or she has been
rehabilitated; and
(k) fulfils other conditions required for the
office for which he or she seeks to stand
as a candidate.

articles.heading: Incompatible elective offices (1) It is prohibited for any elected person to hold concurrently any two of the following
Period for submission of candidacies
Absence of a candidate for elective position Where no candidacy is received in respect of any elective office, the Commission gives
articles.text:
notice to the public concerned to that effect,
and the period for submission of candidacies
is reopened within 30 days from the date of
such notice, whereupon the election is
conducted in accordance with the provisions
of this Organic Law.
45

articles.heading: Publication of approved candidacies (1) Approved candidacies are published at least seven days before the
articles.text:
commencement of the electoral campaign,
unless otherwise provided by this Organic
Law.
(2) Instructions of the Commission determine
the procedures for the publication of
candidacies.

articles.heading: Withdrawal of candidacy (1)A person having submitted his or her candidacy has the right to withdraw it at
articles.text:
any time prior to the commencement of
polling.
(2)Instructions of the Commission determine
the procedures for withdrawal of
candidacy.

articles.heading: Period and procedures for electoral campaign (1) Any candidate is entitled to conduct an electoral campaign during such a period as
articles.text:
prescribed by the competent organs.
46
(2) Instructions of the Commission determine
the procedures for the conduct of electoral
campaign operations for each category of
election.

articles.heading: Conduct of meetings or rallies during electoral campaign During the electoral campaign, meetings or
articles.text:
rallies related thereto are held freely, subject
to the observance of public order, laws and
regulations.

articles.heading: Candidate’s right to use posters and other electoral campaign materials Unless otherwise provided by this Organic
articles.text:
Law, a candidate has the right to use posters
and other electoral campaign materials,
provided that no such materials are contrary to
this Organic Law.

articles.heading: Prohibited acts during electoral campaign During an electoral campaign conducted on his or her own behalf or on behalf of a third
articles.text:
party, no person is authorised to engage in any
of the following acts for the purpose of
47
influencing, or attempting to influence, the
opinion of a voter:
(a) unlawful use of State property;
(b) any form of insulting or defamatory
statement directed against another
candidate;
(c) act of bribery;
(d) any form of discrimination or
divisionism.

articles.heading: Prohibited acts by candidate on the eve of polling and on polling day On the eve of polling and on polling day, and
articles.text:
unless otherwise provided, a candidate is
prohibited from –
(a) engaging in any activity related to
electoral campaign; and
(b) being present in the vicinity of a
polling station, except for the purpose
of voting or during vote counting.
48
Section 3: Organisation of voting
operations
Subsection One: Polling station and polling
officers in polling stations

articles.heading: Designation and location of polling stations (1) Polling stations are established in public
articles.text:
buildings, premises used for the provision
of public services or such other locations
as designated by the Commission.
(2) For the purposes of the presidential
election, direct legislative election and
referendum, polling stations outside
Rwanda are established wherever there is
an Embassy of Rwanda. The Ambassador
may, upon authorisation from the
Commission, establish polling stations at
such other locations as fall within the
territorial jurisdiction of the Embassy.
(3) The Commission determines the location
and number of polling stations as well as
the rooms comprising each polling station,
at least 15 days prior to the polling date.
49

articles.heading: Polling officers at polling stations and in rooms of a polling station (1) The presiding officer of a polling station
articles.text:
is responsible for the coordination of
voting operations at the polling station.
(2) The polling room coordinator and poll
clerks are responsible for voting
operations within the polling room.
(3) Instructions of the Commission
determine the respective responsibilities
of the presiding officer of a polling
station, the polling room coordinator and
the poll clerks.

articles.heading: Swearing-in of polling officers at the polling station Prior to the commencement of polling,
articles.text:
members of the polling station take, before the
members of the public present, the oath
prescribed for officials under the Constitution
of the Republic of Rwanda.
51
accreditation certificate referred to in
Paragraph (2)(b).

articles.heading: Representation of a candidate in the polling room and at polling station
Voting operations a candidate’s agent is authorised to observe (1) A candidate’s agent is entitled to observe
articles.text:
various voting operations except those
taking place in the polling booth.
(2) Irregularities identified by a candidate’s
agent are recorded by the agent in a written
statement signed by the agent, a copy of
which is thereupon delivered to the polling
room coordinator and a further copy
transmitted to the candidate whom the
agent represents.
(3) The polling room coordinator records, in a
written statement, any observations
submitted to him or her in accordance with
the provisions of Paragraph (2). Only
observations so recorded are admissible as
evidence in support of any subsequent
electoral dispute.
52

articles.heading: Accreditation of electoral observers (1)Electoral observers are accredited by the Commission upon application
articles.text:
(2)Instructions of the Commission determine
the period for receiving applications and
accrediting electoral observers.

articles.heading: Rights of an electoral observer and candidate’s agent An electoral observer and candidate’s agent
Obligations of an electoral observer and candidate’s agent (1) An electoral observer and candidate’s
articles.text:
agent comply with the following:
(a) to refrain from any activity that
may disrupt the orderly conduct of
the electoral process;
(b) to refrain from impartiality in the
conduct of electoral operations;
(c) to comply with the provisions of
national laws in force, in general,
and legislation relating to
elections, in particular;
(d) to respect the national culture;
(e) to refrain from giving orders to
polling officers;
54
(f) to operate only in the geographical
area for which they have been
accredited;
(g) to accord due respect to polling
officers at all levels;
(h) to refrain from proclamation of
election results prior to
proclamation thereof by the
competent authority.
(2) In particular, an electoral observer
produces a report based on the factual
observations made in the course of the
election and submits it to the
Commission, within 60 days from the
close of the poll.
Subsection 3: Ballot box and ballot papers

articles.heading: Preparation and use of a ballot box (1) Prior to the commencement of voting, the polling officers exhibit to the public,
articles.text:
candidates’ agents and electoral
observers, if any, the ballot box, fitted
with a single slot for the insertion of
55
ballot papers and opened for verification
that it is empty. The ballot box is
thereafter sealed before the opening of
the poll and remain sealed until the
commencement of vote counting. Upon
completion of vote counting, it is
resealed with the used ballot papers
contained therein.
(2) The ballot box is positioned in a
location that is visible to every person
present in the voting room.
(3) Instructions of the Commission
determine the procedures for the
sealing of the ballot box.

articles.heading: Format of a ballot paper and counting of ballot papers for use in the voting room (1) Instructions of the Commission
articles.text:
determine the format and use of the
ballot paper.
(2) Prior to the commencement of voting,
polling officers count the number of
ballot papers issued to them and the
number of such ballot papers is
recorded in a written statement.
56
Subsection 4: Duration of polling and
polling procedures

articles.heading: Duration of polling (1) Polling is conducted over a single day for each category of election. However, where
articles.text:
justified grounds for postponement exist,
the Commission takes such other
arrangements as are necessary to that
effect.
(2) Polling opens at 7:00 a.m. and closes at
3:00 p.m. for a direct election. For an
indirect election, the opening and closing
hours of polling are determined by
instructions of the Commission.
(3) In the event that a ground for delay in the
opening or closing of polling arises, the
electoral committee may modify the
opening and closing hours of polling, upon
prior notification to and consultation with
the chairperson of the Commission.

articles.heading: Voting procedures (1) Voting is conducted by secret ballot, unless otherwise provided for by this
articles.text:
Organic Law.
57
(2) Voting is exercised freely and
transparently, and no person may be
subjected to any coercion or to any form of
influence whatsoever of a nature to get him
or her to modify his or her choice of vote.
(3) Voting may be by direct or indirect
suffrage under the conditions determined
for each category of election.
(4) Voting is expressed by means of a ballot
paper, by a voter lining up behind the
candidate of his or her choice, or by such
other method as may be determined by the
Commission.
(5) Voting by means of a ballot paper is
exercised by the affixing of a fingerprint or
by means of a pen.
(6) Instructions of the Commission determine
the procedures for the implementation of
the provisions of this Article.

articles.heading: Electoral college quorum for the commencement of indirect voting (1) Indirect voting starts when the quorum of
articles.text:
the electoral college reaches at least an
absolute majority of its members.
58
(2) Where an absolute majority is not obtained
on the polling day, a new ballot is
conducted within seven days. Where, at
the close of the second ballot, an absolute
majority is not obtained, the ballot is
conducted irrespective of the number of
the members present.
(3) Instructions of the Commission determine
the date for the resumption of the ballot
provided for under Paragraph (2).

articles.heading: Tranquillity of voting operation Voting is conducted in tranquillity. No person carrying a weapon is permitted to enter the
articles.text:
polling room, except where a security officer
has been requisitioned by the presiding officer
of the polling station for the purpose of
restoring order in the event of a disturbance of
security.

articles.heading: Casting of a single vote and in the polling booth A person casts his or her vote only once
articles.text:
Voting takes place in the polling booth, except
as otherwise provided under this Organic Law.
61

articles.heading: Signatory to written statements of voting operations in the polling room
Resolution of an issue arising in the polling room or at the polling station
Person authorised to vote at a place other than that of his or her registration
Suspension of voting operations in the event of exhaustion of voting materials In the event of exhaustion of certain polling
articles.text:
materials while voters are still present, the
ongoing voting operations are immediately
suspended and the persons present are
informed thereof. Voting operations resume as
soon as such materials become available
again, and a record thereof is entered in a
written statement.

articles.heading: Marks indicating a person having voted (1) After casting his or her vote and depositing the ballot paper in the ballot
articles.text:
box, the voter receives the marks
indicating that he or she has voted.
(2) Instructions of the Commission determine
the marks indicating a person having voted
and procedures for their application.
Subsection 5: Counting and collection of
votes
62

articles.heading: Commencement of vote counting and officers in charge of vote counting (1) Vote counting commences immediately
articles.text:
after the close of the poll in each polling
room.
(2) Vote counting is conducted publicly by the
poll clerks, in the presence of the public,
electoral observers, as well as candidates
or their agents, if any.

articles.heading: Order of vote counting operations (1) Vote counting operations are conducted in the following order
articles.text:
(a) to confirm and proclaim the number of
voters registered on the voters’ register
who have voted;
(b) to publicly proceed with the opening of
the ballot box;
(c) to proceed with the counting of the
ballot papers contained in the ballot
box and proclaim their number;
63
(d) one of the poll clerks hands the
unfolded ballot paper to a second poll
clerk, who reads it aloud;
(e) the vote indicated on the ballot paper is
recorded by a third poll clerk on a tally
sheet established for that purpose and
displayed in full view of all persons
present, or in accordance with any
other procedure prescribed by the
Commission;
(f) upon completion of the reading aloud
of all ballot papers, the votes cast in
favour of each candidate or list of
candidates are counted on the basis of
the valid ballot papers, and any invalid
ballot papers are, if any, counted
separately;
(g) poll clerks approve the contents of the
tally sheets by affixing their signatures
thereto, the signatures of those who
counted the votes being preceded by
their full names and national identity
card numbers;
(h) the candidates or their agents present
may also affix their signatures to the
tally sheets; however, the absence of
such signatures does not, under any
64
circumstances, give rise to the nullity
of the vote counting results;
(i) the declaration of the vote counting
results takes place immediately upon
completion of vote counting.
(j) the polling officers assigned to the
polling station centralize all vote
counting results;
(k) the polling room coordinator and the
poll clerks draw up, without
adjournment, a written statement of
voting operations in two copies on the
forms prescribed for that purpose,
which contain the following:
(i) the time of opening and closing of
the poll, the completion of the
various formalities prescribed by
this Organic Law and, where
applicable, any incidents having
occurred during the voting
operations;
(ii) the signatures of the polling
officers assigned to the polling
station and those of the candidates
65
or their agents, if any;
(iii)the failure by the candidates or
their agents to affix their signatures
to a written statement does not
constitute a ground for its
invalidation.
(l) candidates’ agents have the right to
observe all vote counting operations
and to request that their observations
or objections be entered in a written
statement;
(m)the polling room coordinator draws up
a written statement in two copies, one
of which is placed by him or her in a
sealed envelope which is, together
with valid, unused and invalid ballot
papers, deposited in the ballot box of
the polling room, and subsequently
transmitted by him or her to the
presiding officer of the polling station;
with the other copy being handed to the
presiding officer of the polling station;
(n) the presiding officer of the polling
station consolidates the results on the
basis of the written statements received
from the polling stations, draws up a
66
corresponding written statement which
he or she places, in public, in a sealed
and stamped envelope, and
subsequently transmits the said written
statement to the electoral coordinator
at the District level through the
intermediary of the coordinator of
voting operations at the Sector level;
and such written statement must
contain the following:
(i) the number of persons
registered on the voters’
register and authorised to
vote;
(ii) the number of those having
cast their votes;
(iii) the number of persons having
voted at the polling station
without being registered on
the voters’ register of that
polling station;
(iv) the number of ballot papers
received;
(v) the number of valid and
invalid ballot papers;
67
(vi) the number of complaint
forms, if any;
(vii) the number of tally sheets;
(viii) the number of unused ballot
papers.
(2) Where more than one election is held on
the same day, instructions of the
Commission determine the election to take
precedence in vote counting.

articles.heading: Criteria for the invalidity of a ballot paper (1) A ballot paper is invalid where – (a) it does not comply with this Organic
articles.text:
Law or instructions of the
Commission;
(b) it bears signs other than those
prescribed for use;
(c) it does not clearly indicate the
candidate voted for;
(d) the voter reveals his or her identity
on the ballot paper;
68
(e) it is deposited in the ballot box
without any expression of the vote;
or
(f) it bears markings other than those
prescribed.
(2) Invalid ballot papers do not constitute
valid votes cast and are not taken into
account in calculating the percentage
of votes obtained by a candidate.

articles.heading: Procedures for the consolidation of election results (1) At each level, the electoral coordinator
articles.text:
consolidates election results and
communicates them to electoral
observers, candidates’ agents,
journalists and the public, where
present.
(2) The consolidation of election results at
the level of the various administrative
entities of the country is carried out in
accordance with the instructions of the
Commission.
(3) The consolidated election result sheet
is posted at the place where the
69
operation was carried out. The format
of that document and the place of its
posting are determined by the
instructions of the Commission.
(4) The Chairperson of the Commission
consolidates the election results at the
national level on the basis of the
consolidated tally sheets.

articles.heading: Collection and preservation of ballot papers In accordance with the instructions of the Commission, ballot papers used during voting
articles.text:
operations are collected and preserved by the
electoral coordinator at the District level until
the proclamation of the final results.

articles.heading: Declaration of a sole candidate as elected (1) When an election is contested by a sole candidate, that candidate is declared
articles.text:
elected upon obtaining an absolute
majority of the valid votes cast.
(2) Where the candidate is not declared
elected, a new ballot is held within 90
days from the proclamation of the
election results, in accordance with the
70
provisions of this Organic Law.
(3) Where, in the new ballot referred to in
paragraph (2), there is again only one
candidate, that candidate is declared
elected regardless of the number of votes
obtained.

articles.heading: Commencement of the term of office of elected persons The term of office of elected persons at all
articles.text:
levels provided for under this Organic Law
who are required to take an oath of office takes
effect from the day on which they take the oath
of office provided for under the Constitution
of the Republic of Rwanda.

articles.heading: Candidate elected without meeting required conditions If, after the proclamation of the final election
articles.text:
results, it appears at any time that a candidate
whose candidacy had been accepted and who
was elected did not fulfil the required
conditions, his or her election is annulled by
the competent court upon application by any
interested party. However, any acts performed
by that person in the exercise of the functions
to which he or she had been elected remain
valid.
72
(b) consists of a combination of the
colours of the national flag;
(c) is likely to cause divisions;
(d) may create confusion; or
(e) has been chosen by another
candidate.
(2) Where several candidates, political
organisations or coalitions of political
organisations choose the same acronym or
symbol, the Commission makes a final
decision assigning the use of that acronym

national television is concerned.

(1) Where a candidate appearing on the list of
a political organisation or a coalition of
political organisations fails to comply with
the law during the electoral campaign, the
Commission summons the political
78
organisation or coalition of political
organisations concerned for the purpose of
issuing it with an official verbal warning.
(2) Where the candidate found to be in
violation of the law fails to comply with
the warning issued to him or her, the
Commission issues to his or her political
organisation or coalition of political
organisations a final written warning.
(3) Where the same violation of the law
persists, the Commission requires the
political organisation or coalition of
political organisations concerned to
remove the candidate concerned from
its list within 12 hours of the written
notification of a further misconduct
committed by the latter.
(4) Where the political organisation or
coalition of political organisations fails
to remove the candidate from its list, the
Commission decides to remove the
candidate from the list within 24 hours

organisation or coalition of political

political organisations, the Senate, the

Supreme Court, as well as the

(5) A candidate removed from the list of

within a period not exceeding 24 hours

candidates. However, such proceedings
have no suspensive effect on the
electoral process.
(6) Any political organisation or coalition
of political organisation that violates the

campaign is prosecuted in accordance
with the relevant legislation.

articles.heading: Proclamation of election results and related time limit (1) The Commission proclaims election

articles.heading: Petition relating to the filing of a candidacy and to the presidential or legislative election
articles.text:
(1) Any interested Rwandan or any candidate
has the right to seise the competent court
of a petition relating to the filing of a
candidacy and to the presidential or
legislative election.
(2) Any person wishing to file the petition
referred to in Paragraph (1) does so within
48 hours of the provisional publication by
the Commission of the list of candidates or
of the election results.
(3) No petition may have suspensive effect on
the ongoing electoral process, except for a
petition relating to the proclamation of the
final results.
81

articles.heading: Proclamation of election results in case of rectification Where the competent court orders the
articles.text:

Commission proclaims the final election
results on the basis of the court decision.
Section 2: Specific provisions applicable to

Subsection One: Submission of candidacy

articles.heading: Submission of candidacy for the office of President of the Republic (1) The submission of a candidacy for the
articles.text:
office of President of the Republic is
made in writing, in an individual
capacity, and is lodged with the
Commission against an
acknowledgement of receipt.
(2) The documents required from the
candidate are submitted in two copies,
one of which is retained by the
Commission, while the other, bearing the
stamp of the Commission on each page, is
82
returned to the candidate.
(3) The submission of candidacy for the
office of President of the Republic is
effected at least 45 days before the polling
date.

articles.heading: Constituent elements of the candidacy file for the office of President of the Republic (1) The candidacy file for the office of
articles.text:
President of the Republic comprises the
following elements:
(a) a declaration of candidature indicating –
(i) the candidate’s full name as it appears
on the national identity card; and
(ii) that the candidate is nominated by a
legally constituted political
organisation or by a legally constituted
coalition of political organisations, or
that he or she stands as an independent
candidate, or as a candidate sponsored
by several political organisations.
83
(b) a curriculum vitae indicating –
(i) his or her occupation;
(ii) his or her place of
residence; and
(iii)his or her previously-held
positions.
(c) a copy of his or her national identity
card;
(d) two passport-sized colour photographs;
(e) the candidate’s written declaration
stating that he or she does not hold any
other nationality or that he or she has
renounced any other nationality
previously held;
(f) a birth certificate issued by the
competent authority;
(g) a certificate of good conduct issued by
the competent authority;
(h) a valid criminal record certificate issued
by the competent authority;
84
(i) a certificate by which a political
organisation or a coalition of political
organisations declares its sponsorship of
the candidate concerned for the
presidential election;
(j) a declaration of assets certificate where
the candidate is among persons subject
to the obligation to declare assets;
(k) a medical certificate issued by a
recognised medical doctor;
(l) his or her distinguishing symbol
intended to appear on the ballot paper;
and
(m)a written declaration by the candidate,
bearing his or her signature or
fingerprint, attesting to the authenticity
of the required documents submitted.
(2) The provisions of Paragraph (1)(i) apply to
candidates nominated by political
organisations or a coalition of political
organisations.
85

articles.heading: Other specific requirements in support of the candidacy of an independent candidate (1) The independent candidate submits a list
articles.text:

his or her candidacy, comprising at least
600 voters registered on the voters’
register, including at least 12 persons per

(2) The list of persons supporting the
independent candidate indicates, in

the national identity card;
(b) the number of his or her national
identity card;
(c) his or her place of domicile;
(d) his or her place of registration on
voters’ register;
(e) his or her signature or fingerprint.
(3) Instructions of the Commission
determine the time limits and procedures
86
in accordance with which an
independent candidate prepares the list
of persons eligible to vote supporting his
or her candidacy.
Subsection 2: Presidential election

articles.heading: Electoral constituency applicable to the presidential election The electoral constituency applicable to the
articles.text:
presidential election extends to the entire
national territory. However, Rwandans
residing abroad are authorised to vote from
their place of residence, in accordance with the
provisions of this Organic Law.

articles.heading: Procedures applicable to the conduct of the presidential election (1) The election of the President of the
articles.text:
Republic is by direct universal suffrage
through a secret ballot.
(2) In the presidential election, voters cast
their votes for one candidate in a single
round of voting.
(3) The candidate having obtained the highest
number of votes is declared President of
the Republic. In the event of an equality of
87
votes between the leading candidates, a
new election is conducted between the
candidates concerned only, within 30 days
from the date of the proclamation of final
results of the first election.
Section 3: Specific provisions applicable to
the election of Deputies
Subsection One: Submission of candidacy
for the office of Deputy

articles.heading: Procedures for submission of candidacy (1) Any person wishing to stand as a candidate for the office of Deputy submits an
articles.text:
individual candidacy for one seat only in
the election of Deputies.
(2) No person is authorised to submit his or her
candidacy simultaneously for a direct
election and for an indirect election.
(3) The candidacy is submitted to the
Commission, at least 45 days prior to the
polling day.
(4) The Commission issues an
acknowledgement of receipt. However,
88
such acknowledgement of receipt does not
constitute a determination as to the
admissibility of the candidacy submitted.
(5) Instructions of the Commission determine
the procedures for submission and receipt
of candidacy.

articles.heading: Submission of list of candidates of political organisations or coalition of political organisations
articles.text:
(1) A political organisation or a coalition of
political organisations submits a closed
list of candidates.
(2) The closed list comprises not more than
80 candidates. At least 30% of the
candidates appearing on the closed list
must be female
(3) The representative of a political
organisation or a coalition of political
organisations submits to the Commission
the list of candidates, their respective
files, and a power of attorney authorising
him or her to represent the political
organisation or the coalition of political
organisations. In the event of the
representative’s unavailability, such
formality may be carried out by another
person mandated by him or her.
89
(4) The list of candidates of a political
organisation or a coalition of political
organisations is accompanied by –
(a) a written statement bearing the
names and signatures of the
members of the supreme organ of
the political organisation or the
coalition of political organisations
having adopted the said list in
accordance with the law; and
(b) the distinguishing symbol of the
political organisation or the
coalition of political organisations
intended to appear on the ballot
paper.

articles.heading: Replacement of a Deputy elected from the list of a political organisation or a coalition of political organisations
articles.text:
(1) Where a Deputy ceases to hold office, he
or she is replaced in accordance with the
order of presentation of candidates
appearing on the list on which he or she
was elected. The seat is allocated to the
next candidate on the said list, who serves
the remainder of the term of office where
such remainder exceeds one year.
(2) However, where there exist grounds
preventing the application of the
provisions of Paragraph (1), the political
organisation or coalition of political
organisations informs the Commission
thereof in writing, stating such grounds,
within five days from the date on which
the Deputy concerned ceased to hold
office.
104
(3) Where a Deputy elected from the list of a
political organisation or a coalition of
political organisations ceases to hold
office for any reason whatsoever, the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies
notifies the Commission thereof in order
for the latter to announce the name of the
Deputy who is to replace him or her.
(4) The Commission makes public to the
Rwandans the name of the new Deputy
within seven days from the date of
notification by the Speaker of the Chamber
of Deputies.
(5) In the event of dissolution of a political
organisation, or where one or more
Deputies resign and no replacement
appears on the list, new elections are
organised in order to replace those
Deputies having resigned within 90 days
from the date of notification to the
Commission. In such case, each political
organisation, as well as independent
candidates, may submit candidatures for
the vacant seat in accordance with the
ordinary procedures applicable when such
seats are open for electoral contest.

for the office of Senator

articles.heading: Submission of candidacies for Senators elected according to national administrative entities and from

14

articles.heading: Documents accompanying candidacies for Senators elected in accordance with national administrative
articles.text:
entities and from institutions of higher
learning

articles.heading: Specific conditions applicable to candidates in the election of Senators elected from institutions of higher learning
articles.text:
(1) Candidates in the election of Senators
elected from public and private
institutions of higher learning must be
permanent members of the teaching or
research staff within such institutions and
hold, at a minimum, the academic rank of
associate professor.
(2) A person wishing to stand as a candidate
in the election of Senators elected from
public or private institutions of higher
learning submits to the Commission the
following:
(a) a certificate of permanent
employment issued by a public or
private institution of higher learning,
as the case may be;
(b) a document certifying that he or she
has been appointed to at least the
rank of Associate Professor.
(3) Where a Senator previously elected from
institutions of higher learning wishes to
stand for a second term of office in the
110
same capacity, he or she is not required to
submit the document provided for under
Paragraph (2)(a) where the term sought is
consecutive to his or her current term of
office.

articles.heading: Approval of the list of candidates for elected Senators (1) Candidacies for elected Senator are
articles.text:
approved by the Supreme Court.
(2) The Commission submits to the
Supreme Court, for approval, the
candidacy files received from
candidates for the office of Senator,
together with the list of candidates and
its assessment of each candidacy,
within three days from the date of
closure of the reception of candidacies.
(3) The written request submitted to the
Supreme Court for the approval of
candidacies for the office of Senator is
deemed to constitute a petition filed
with the Court. The Supreme Court
examines and approves, in camera, the
candidacies submitted to it, sitting as a
bench composed of at least two-thirds
of its judges, on the basis of the
documents and other conditions
required by law for candidates for the
111
office of Senator. The decision of the
Supreme Court is not subject to appeal.
(4) Within five days from receipt of the
candidacy files for the office of
Senator, the Chief Registrar of the
Supreme Court transmits to the
Commission the list of approved
candidates and the list of non-approved
candidates, together with their
respective files, and the Commission
officially publish the list of approved
candidates within 24 hours from the
time of receipt of such list transmitted
by the Supreme Court.
(5) The candidacy files for the office of
Senator are stored in an archive at the
Commission.

articles.heading: Approval of the list of senatorial candidates nominated by the National Consultative Forum of Political
articles.text:
Organisations
(1) After nominating Senatorial candidates,
the National Consultative Forum of
Political Organisations submits to the
Supreme Court, for approval, the
112
candidacy files of such candidates within
three days from the date of their
designation by the Forum.
(2) The written request submitted to the
Supreme Court for the approval of
candidacies for the office of Senator is
deemed to constitute a petition filed with
the Supreme Court.
(3) The consideration of candidacies by the
Supreme Court is conducted in camera,
sitting as a bench composed of at least
two-thirds of its judges, solely on the
basis of the documents and conditions
required by law for candidates for the
office of Senator. The decision of the
Supreme Court is not subject to appeal.
(4) After rendering its decision, the Chief
Registrar of the Supreme Court transmits
to the National Consultative Forum of
Political Organisations the list of
candidates approved for the office of
Senator and the list of candidates not
approved, together with their respective
files. The National Consultative Forum of
Political Organisations thereafter
transmits to the Senate the list of
approved Senators within 24 hours from
117
notification to the Commission. Such election
is conducted in accordance with the provisions
of this Organic Law.

paper.

competent authority implements it.

119

articles.heading: Organisation and conduct of election for Rwandans living abroad The provisions of this Organic Law relating to
articles.text:
the organisation and conduct of the
presidential election, the election of Deputies
elected by direct suffrage, and the referendum
apply in full to the election for Rwandans
living abroad.

articles.heading: Transmission of the final voters’ register Once the final voters’ register has been established, the Ambassador immediately
articles.text:
transmits it to the Commission, together with
a closing report on the compilation of the
voters’ register, through the means of
communication determined by the
Commission.
120

articles.heading: Number of polling stations A polling station is established at each embassy. However, at the request of the

Ambassador, the Commission may establish
additional polling stations within the
jurisdiction of that embassy in order to
facilitate voters.

articles.heading: Written statements of the close of the poll and of vote counting Written statements of the close of the poll and

of vote counting are transmitted to the
Commission within 48 hours following the
close of the poll, through the means of
communication determined by the
Commission.

Section One: Common provisions

articles.heading: Elective leadership positions at the level of decentralised administrative entities (1) The election of leaders of elective
Means used during electoral campaign (1) The electoral campaign is conducted by means of speeches, photographs, written
articles.text:
materials and technologies during the
period prescribed for that purpose.
(2) Instructions of the Commission
determine the procedures for the
implementation of the provisions of
Paragraph (1).

articles.heading: Prohibited Acts for candidates for leadership positions in decentralised administrative entities
articles.text:
During the electoral campaign period, the
following acts are prohibited:
(a) conducting an electoral campaign for a
leadership position in the name of a
political organisation;
(b) posting photographs, written materials,
and conducting any other electoral
campaign activity in an unauthorised
place;
(c) using the national symbols and
emblems of political organisations on a
123
candidate’s electoral campaign
photographs and written materials.

articles.heading: Decision taken against a candidate conducting an electoral campaign in violation of the law
articles.text:
Without prejudice to the provisions of other
laws, any candidate who conducts an electoral
campaign in violation of the provisions of this
Organic Law is issued with a warning and, in
the event of failure to comply with such
warning, is removed from the list of
candidates.

articles.heading: Being declared elected (1) At the level at which the election is conducted, the candidates obtaining the
articles.text:
highest number of valid votes cast are
declared elected, having regard to the
number of positions to be filled.
(2) However, where candidates obtain an
equal number of votes and are competing
for a single position, a new ballot is
conducted between the tied candidates
within three days from the date of
proclamation of the results of the first
ballot.
124
(3) A new ballot may be conducted only
once. Where the tie persists, the elected
candidate is determined by drawing lots.
(4) Instructions of the Commission
determine the procedures for the conduct
of a new ballot and the drawing of lots.

articles.heading: Replacement of elected persons (1) Where a person elected to office is unable to continue exercising the
articles.text:
functions for which he or she was
elected, and where the unexpired term
of office is at least one year, such person
is replaced through an election.
(2) However, where several elected
persons are unable to continue
exercising their functions to such an
extent that decision-making by majority
is rendered impossible, they are
replaced through an election,
irrespective of the remaining duration
of the term of office provided for under
Paragraph (1) of this Article.
(3) The Minister in charge of local
government notifies the Commission,
within 30 days from the date on which
125
the person concerned ceased to hold the
office to which he or she had been
elected, of the vacancy requiring the
organisation of an election for his or her
replacement.
(4) An election intended to replace a leader
who has ceased to exercise the
functions for which he or she had been
elected is organised within 60 days
from the date of notification to the
Commission.
(5) Where, upon the expiry of the term of
office of an elected person, a case of
force majeure prevents the conduct of
the election, the holder of such office
remains in office until the cessation of
the case of force majeure.
(6) The Minister in charge of local
government, after consultation with the
Commission, issues an Order
postponing the election on grounds of
force majeure. The cessation of the case
of force majeure is announced by an
Order of the same Minister.
(7) In the event of force majeure or any other
circumstance rendering the holding of an
election impossible within the framework
of a process provided for under this
126
Organic Law, an Order issued by the
Minister in charge of local government,
after consultation with the Commission,
may prescribe alternative procedures for
the conduct of such election.

articles.heading: Procedures for the election of leaders at the Village, Cell and Sector levels The election of leaders at the Village, Cell and
articles.text:
Sector levels may be conducted by non-secret
ballot.

articles.text:
conditions required for candidates for
leadership positions at the Village, Cell, and
Sector levels, as well as the members of the
electoral colleges at each level.

articles.heading: Settlement of issues related to the electoral process (1) During the election of leaders at the
articles.text:
127
Village, Cell, and Sector levels, any issue
arising from voting operations is
immediately referred to the electoral
supervisor at the relevant level, who
determines the matter without delay in a
public session, in the presence of citizens
present at the polling venue, and records

articles.heading: Election of general councillors and female councillors at the District level (1) At the district level, general
articles.text:
councillors, as well as female

articles.heading: Election of members of the Council elected within a District of the City of Kigali (1) Members of the Council of the City of

City of Kigali are elected by indirect

Kigali
The submission of candidacies for the office
of member of the Executive Committee of
District and of the City of Kigali takes place
on the polling day before the members of the

articles.heading: Procedures for the election of members of the Executive Committee of District and of the City of Kigali
articles.text:
The election of members of the Executive
Committee of the District and of the City of
135
Kigali is conducted by indirect and secret
ballot.

Executive Committee of District or of the
City of Kigali
(1) A person wishing to submit his or her
candidacy for the office of member of
the Executive Committee of District or
of the City of Kigali must–

District Council or of the Council

A Presidential Order determines members of

Council

(1) A candidate for the office of member of

(b) be at least 25 years of age; and
(c) hold at least a bachelor’s degree

authority.

articles.heading: Competent organs for the settlement of disputes relating to candidacies (1) A person dissatisfied with a decision
articles.text:
taken in respect of his or her candidacy
by the level of the Commission having
received such candidacy may lodge an
appeal before the hierarchically superior
organ within 24 hours from the taking of
such decision.
(2) The decision taken by the appellate
organ states the grounds upon which it is
based and is rendered within 48 hours
from receipt of the appeal.
139
(3) The decision taken by the Commission
at the national level may be referred to
the competent court within 24 hours
from the taking of such decision.
However, such referral does not have
suspensive effect on the conduct of the
electoral process.

articles.heading: Competent organ to hear informal appeal in the event of a dispute relating to election results
articles.text:
(1) At first instance, any person contesting
the election results immediately refers
the matter to the organ of the
Commission at the level at which the
election was conducted, upon the
proclamation of the election results.
The decision is rendered without delay
and made public.
(2) The decision rendered states the
grounds on which it is based and is
recorded in a written statement signed
by both parties.
(3) Instructions of the Commission
determine the format of the written
140
statement provided for under
Paragraph (2).

articles.heading: Organ seized of hierarchical appeals (1) Where the appellant is dissatisfied with the decision rendered by the organ at
articles.text:
the level at which the election was
conducted, he or she may lodge a
written appeal before the Commission

the said decision.
(2) The Commission rules on the appeal

appeal.

articles.text:
(1) A person who, during an electoral

commits an offence. Upon conviction,

articles.heading: Misconduct of a member of the electoral college aimed at disrupting electoral operations (1) A member of the electoral college who,

articles.heading: Objet de la présente loi organique
Interprétation Dans la présente loi organique
articles.text:
(a) « Ambassade du Rwanda » comprend
tout lieu situé sur le territoire relevant de
la circonscription de la mission
diplomatique du Rwanda à l’étranger ;
(b) « Ambassadeur » signifie un
représentant du Rwanda auprès d’un État
étranger ;
(c) « proclamation des résultats de
l’élection » signifie une annonce
officielle des résultats d’élection faite par
l’autorité compétente après consolidation
des résultats du scrutin recueillis à tous
les échelons où s’est déroulé le scrutin ;
(d) « bureau de vote » signifie une structure
désignée par la Commission qui
comporte au moins une salle de vote ;
(e) « salle de vote » signifie une salle
désignée par la Commission dans laquelle
les personnes admises à voter et inscrites
sur la liste électorale expriment leur vote ;
(f) « carte nationale d’identité » signifie un
document physique ou numérique
permettant d’identifier une personne,
délivré par l’autorité compétente ;
(g) « liste électorale » signifie un document
contenant les renseignements personnels
des personnes admises à voter ;
(h) « vote nul » signifie un vote d’un électeur
comportant des signes autres que ceux
prévus pour le vote ou ne comportant
aucune marque ;
(i) « personne expérimentée » signifie une
personne qui, sur une longue période, a
exercé des fonctions substantielles et a
ainsi acquis, par l’exercice de diverses
activités, des compétences ou des
connaissances pertinentes au regard des
attributions attachées à une fonction
élective ;
(j) « observateur électoral » signifie un
citoyen rwandais ou un ressortissant
étranger qui représente une organisation
non gouvernementale nationale, la
Plateforme de la société civile du
Rwanda, une organisation
confessionnelle, un organe étatique, un
État, une organisation internationale ou
étrangère, accrédités par la Commission
nationale électorale aux fins d’observer le
processus électoral ;
(k) « collège électoral » signifie un groupe
de personnes ayant le droit de voter ;
(l) « personne intègre » signifie un citoyen
rwandais irréprochable dans son
comportement et dans ses relations avec
autrui ;
(m)« élection » signifie un processus par
lequel un choix est effectué par voie de
vote ;
(n) «élection directe » signifie un système
électoral par lequel l’électeur exprime
personnellement son vote ;
(o) « élection indirecte » signifie un
système électoral par lequel les personnes
ayant le droit de vote sont représentées,
lors de l’expression du vote, par certaines
d’entre elles ;
(p) « Commission » signifie la Commission
nationale électorale ;
(q) « comité électoral » signifie un comité
composé d’un président du bureau de
vote et de coordinateurs des salles de
vote ;
(r) « déclaration des résultats du scrutin »
signifie l’annonce des résultats du scrutin
au niveau auquel le scrutin est organisé,
effectuée par les personnes chargées de
l’organisation du scrutin à ce niveau ;
(s) « campagne électorale » signifie le
processus par lequel un candidat
indépendant, une organisation politique
ou une coalition d’organisations
politiques assure la promotion de son
programme et le présente en vue de se
faire élire ;
(t) « isoloir » signifie un espace aménagé à
l’intérieur d’une salle de vote aux fins de
permettre à l’électeur d’exprimer son
vote dans le secret ;
(u) « représentant d’un candidat » signifie
un citoyen rwandais inscrit sur la liste
électorale mandaté par un candidat pour
suivre le processus électoral en son nom ;
(v) « coordinateur électoral » signifie une
personne nommée par la Commission
pour assurer, à chaque niveau de la
Commission, la supervision et la
coordination des opérations électorales ;
(w)« candidat » signifie toute personne
physique, formation politique ou
coalition de formations politiques
remplissant les conditions requises qui est
en compétition électorale;
(x) « bénévole électoral » signifie une
personne volontaire et capable nommée
par la Commission pour participer, sans
rémunération, à la préparation et à la
conduite des opérations électorales ;
(y) « assesseur » signifie une personne
chargée des opérations de vote dans une
salle de vote ;
(z) « niveau de la Commission » signifie
une salle de vote, un bureau de vote, un
District, une Province, la Ville de Kigali
ou le pays, au niveau desquels se déroule
le scrutin, ainsi que de tout autre lieu
déterminé par la Commission ;
(aa) « électeur » signifie tout citoyen
rwandais ayant le droit de vote.

articles.heading: Champ d’application La présente loi organique s’applique aux élections suivantes
Organe chargé des élections (1) L’organe chargé des élections est la Commission
articles.text:
(2) La Commission est chargée de veiller
au respect des lois régissant les
élections et d’édicter, si nécessaire, des
instructions requises pour assurer le
bon déroulement des élections
conformément aux dispositions de la

Commission nomme des bénévoles
électoraux.

fixent les modalités de désignation des
bénévoles électoraux ainsi que les
conditions requises pour eux.

Personne non admise à se faire inscrire sur la liste électorale
Agent chargé de l’inscription sur la liste électorale et ses attributions (1) Un bénévole électoral désigné par la

Commission est chargé de l’inscription sur

(a) veiller à ce que l’inscription sur la liste

loi ;
(b) conserver la liste électorale et assurer la
sécurité du matériel en collaboration
avec les autorités du lieu de l’opération

(c) préparer un rapport sur l’opération

articles.heading: Correction de la liste électorale entre la publication de la liste électorale provisoire et celle de la liste définitive
articles.text:
(1) La Commission procède à la correction
des erreurs constatées après la
publication de la liste électorale
provisoire.
(2) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de correction
de la liste électorale pendant la période
comprise entre la publication de la liste
électorale provisoire et celle de la liste
électorale définitive.

articles.heading: Publication de la liste des personnes rayées de la liste électorale (1) La Commission publie, avant la
articles.text:
publication de la liste électorale
définitive, la liste des personnes rayées
de la liste électorale pour les motifs
prévus par l’article 7.
(2) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de
publication de la liste des personnes
rayées de la liste électorale.

articles.heading: Conservation de la liste électorale et personne autorisée à y accéder (1) La liste électorale est conservée dans la
articles.text:
base de données de la Commission. Un
candidat ou toute autre personne
autorisée par la Commission se voit
accorder l’accès à sa copie.
(2) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de
conservation de la liste électorale ainsi
que d’accès à sa copie.

articles.heading: Introduction d’une réclamation relative à l’inscription sur la liste électorale (1) Une personne intéressée peut introduire
articles.text:
une réclamation relative à l’inscription sur
la liste électorale. Toutefois, la
réclamation n’est recevable que si elle est
introduite avant la publication de la liste
électorale définitive.
(2) La réclamation est faite par écrit et
adressée au niveau de la Commission du
lieu où le problème est constaté.
(3) Au niveau de l’Ambassade du Rwanda, la
réclamation est introduite par écrit auprès
du coordinateur électoral.

articles.heading: Modalités de règlement d’une réclamation relative à la liste électorale (1) Le niveau de la Commission saisi d’une
articles.text:
réclamation relative à la liste électorale se
prononce dans les 48 heures à compter de
sa réception. Une copie de la décision est
immédiatement remise à la partie
intéressée et, si nécessaire, la liste
électorale est immédiatement corrigée par
inscription supplémentaire ou radiation
conformément à la décision rendue.
(2) Lorsque l’auteur de la réclamation n’est
pas satisfait de la décision rendue, il forme
recours devant le niveau immédiatement
supérieur de la Commission dans les 24
heures à compter de la notification qui lui
est faite de cette décision.
(3) Au niveau de l’Ambassade du Rwanda,
lorsque l’auteur de la réclamation n’est pas
satisfait de la décision du coordinateur
électoral, il forme recours auprès du
président de la Commission dans les 24
heures à compter de la notification qui lui
est faite de cette décision.

liste électorale ou à sa correction, rendue au
dernier niveau de la Commission, peut faire

Section 2 : Dépôt de candidatures et
campagne électorale

articles.heading: Personne admise à être élue Est admise à être élue une personne qui – (a) a atteint l’âge prescrit par la loi ;
articles.text:
(b) est intègre ;
(c) est inscrite sur la liste électorale ;
(d) n’est pas frappée de restrictions prévues
à l’article 7 ;
(e) n’a pas fait l’objet d’une ordonnance de
placement sous tutelle légale rendue par
une juridiction compétente ;
(f) n’est pas atteinte d’une maladie de
nature à l’empêcher de remplir les
fonctions afférentes au poste auquel elle
désire présenter sa candidature ;
(g) n’est plus en service en tant que membre
des Forces rwandaises de défense,
policier, juge, officier de poursuite
judiciaire, enquêteur, membre du
Service national de renseignements et de
sécurité, du Service correctionnel du
Rwanda ou de l’Organe d’appui à
l’administration du District dans le
maintien de la sécurité ;
(h) n’a pas été à l’origine de la faillite d’une
personne morale qu’elle a dirigée, à
moins qu’elle n’ait fait l’objet de
réhabilitation ;
(i) ne pas avoir été condamnée à une peine
d’emprisonnement égale ou supérieure à
6 mois dans un jugement définitif, à
moins d’avoir été réhabilitée ;
(j) ne pas avoir été révoquée de la fonction
publique, à moins d’avoir été
réhabilitée; et
(k) remplit d’autres conditions requises
pour le poste auquel elle désire présenter
sa candidature.

articles.heading: Absence de candidat à un poste électif Lorsqu’aucune candidature n’est déposée pour une fonction élective, la Commission en
articles.text:
informe le public concerné et il est procédé à
la réouverture de la période de dépôt de
candidatures dans les 30 jours à compter de la
date de cette notification, et l’élection est
ensuite organisée conformément aux
dispositions de la présente loi organique.

articles.heading: Publication des candidatures approuvées (1) Les candidatures approuvées sont rendues publiques au moins sept jours
articles.text:
avant l’ouverture de la campagne
électorale, sauf disposition contraire de la
présente loi organique.
(2) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de publication
des candidatures.

articles.heading: Retrait de la candidature (1)Une personne ayant déposé sa candidature a le droit de la retirer avant l’ouverture du
articles.text:
scrutin.
(2)Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de retrait de la
candidature.

articles.heading: Période et modalités de la campagne électorale (1) Un candidat a le droit de mener sa campagne électorale dans les délais prévus
articles.text:
par les organes compétents.
(2) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les modalités de déroulement
des opérations de la campagne électorale
pour chaque catégorie d’élection.

articles.heading: Déroulement des réunions ou rassemblements pendant la campagne électorale Pendant la campagne électorale, les réunions
articles.text:
ou rassemblements y afférents se tiennent
librement, sous réserve du respect de l’ordre
public, des lois et règlements.

articles.heading: Droit du candidat à l’utilisation d’affiches et autres matériels de campagne électorale À moins que la présente loi organique n’en
articles.text:
dispose autrement, un candidat a le droit
d’utiliser des affiches et autre matériel de
campagne électorale, sous réserve qu’ils ne
soient pas contraires à la présente loi
organique.

articles.heading: Actes interdits pendant la campagne électorale Il est, pendant la campagne électorale en sa
articles.text:
faveur ou en faveur d’autrui, interdit à toute
personne, de se livrer à l’un quelconque des
actes suivants en vue d’influencer ou de tenter
d’influencer l’opinion d’un électeur :
(a) usage illicite des biens de l’État ;
(b) toute forme de déclaration injurieuse ou
diffamatoire à l’encontre d’un autre
candidat ;
(c) corruption ;
(d) toute forme de discrimination ou de
divisionnisme.

articles.heading: Actes interdits au candidat la veille et le jour du scrutin La veille et le jour même du scrutin, sauf
articles.text:
disposition contraire, il est interdit à un
candidat de –
(a) se livrer à toute activité en rapport
avec la campagne électorale ; et
(b) être présent aux abords d’un bureau de
vote, sauf pour exercer son droit de
vote ou lors du dépouillement.
Section 3 : Organisation des opérations de
vote
Sous-section première : Bureau de vote et
agents chargés du scrutin au bureau de vote

articles.heading: Désignation et emplacement des bureaux de vote (1) Les bureaux de vote sont établis dans des
articles.text:
bâtiments publics, des locaux affectés aux
services publics ou dans tout autre lieu
désigné par la Commission.
(2) Aux fins de l’élection présidentielle, de
l’élection législative au suffrage direct et
du référendum, des bureaux de vote situés
à l’extérieur du Rwanda sont établis
partout où se trouve une Ambassade du
Rwanda. L’Ambassadeur peut, sur
autorisation de la Commission, établir des
bureaux de vote en tout autre lieu relevant
du ressort territorial de l’Ambassade.
(3) La Commission arrête l’emplacement et le
nombre des bureaux de vote ainsi que le
nombre de salles de vote pour chaque
bureau de vote, au moins 15 jours avant la
date du scrutin.

articles.heading: Agents chargés du scrutin au bureaux de vote et dans les salles du bureau de vote (1) Le président du bureau de vote est chargé
articles.text:
de coordonner les opérations de vote au
sein du bureau de vote.
(2) Le coordinateur de la salle de vote et les
assesseurs sont chargés de la conduite des
opérations de vote dans chaque salle de
vote.
(3) Les instructions de la Commission
déterminent les attributions respectives
du président du bureau de vote, du
coordinateur de la salle de vote et des
assesseurs.

articles.heading: Prestation de serment des agents chargés du scrutin au bureau de vote Avant le début des opérations de vote, les
articles.text:
membres du bureau de vote prêtent, devant les
membres du public présents, le serment des
autorités prévu par la Constitution de la
République du Rwanda.
